title: Image aspect ratios and object-fit
when: Images in cards, galleries or heroes have mixed shapes, look stretched, or make the layout jump while loading.
inputs: the files and their pixel sizes
prompt:
Goal: Every image slot has a chosen ratio, crops without distortion and reserves its space before the file loads.
Steps:
1. Pick ratios by role: 16 / 9 hero and video, 4 / 3 or 3 / 2 cards, 1 / 1 avatars and product tiles, 3 / 4 portraits.
2. Put width and height attributes with the intrinsic size on every img, plus img { max-width: 100%; height: auto }, so the box is reserved.
3. Fixed slots: aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; width: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 30% keeps faces in frame.
4. Logos and product shots that must not crop: object-fit: contain on a neutral background.
5. Offer srcset (400w, 800w, 1600w) with sizes when several files exist; first visible image eager, the rest loading="lazy".
6. Write alt per image: what it shows and why it matters; decorative images get alt="".
Quality bar:
- No stretched or squashed image.
- No layout shift during load.
- Crops keep the subject visible on phones.
Pitfalls:
- A fixed px height with width 100 percent, which distorts.
- Background images for content photos, which lose alt.
- Huge files shrunk only by CSS.
Verify:
- [ ] Every img has alt, width and height.
- [ ] Slots use aspect-ratio and object-fit.
- [ ] Images after the first are lazy.
- [ ] Logos use contain.
Output: Image rules in style.css and updated img tags in the pages.

examples.input: as fotos dos produtos ficam esticadas e de tamanhos diferentes
examples.output: tiles 1 / 1 with object-fit cover, logos contain, width and height on each img, lazy after the first row
